## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 24 user-facing changes.
### New
- Passwords can make one-time codes. Set one up from the site's QR code, a pasted key or link, an image, or the iPhone camera, and Crest offers the live code in the code field, across split fields too. - Crest fills addresses and payment cards into whole forms, menus included, and offers to save new ones you send. They're shared by every Space, and a card fills only after Touch ID or your device password. - On sites that ask for your email or username first, choosing an account fills its password on the next page as soon as it appears. - Settings › Autofill › Passwords has Add Password, for a password you type in yourself, with a strong password one click away.
### Improved
- When a password manager extension handles passwords in a Space, Crest leaves passwords and codes to it and says so once. Addresses and cards still fill. - The engine's own password, payment and address settings pages open Settings › Autofill instead. - Clicking anywhere on the page outside the field closes Crest's passwords popup. - Saved passwords show each site's own icon in Settings and in the popup, fetched once from the site itself when Crest hasn't seen it yet. - The sidebar scrolls smoothly with hundreds or thousands of tabs, and tab icons no longer pop in as rows scroll into view.
### Fixed
- Logins saved for an IP address written another way, such as 127.1, fill again. - On Chromium pages, only Crest offers to save and fill passwords, even if the engine's own password setting was turned back on. - On Chromium pages, suggestions point at sign-in fields inside a frame from another site, and follow the page as it scrolls.

## Highlights
Crest 0.11 has a new look: a new mark and app icons, warm paper, Crest blue and the Allo typeface. It brings Site Controls to Mac, iPhone and iPad, a new setup, and Space looks made from a template, colors and an icon. Crest for Mac now runs on Intel Macs and on macOS 15 Sequoia, with Chromium 158.
### Added
- Setting up Crest is a short walkthrough beside a live preview of the window you're building: bring tabs from another browser, choose your first Space's name, template, colors and icon, add more Spaces and Sub-Spaces, then make Crest your default browser and choose its search and ad blocking in Make It Home. Tabs and folders you close, move or file in the preview stay that way when you start browsing. - Site Controls gather the page's actions and the site's settings in one place: the page and its connection, the actions you use most on top, extensions, ads and trackers, Reader, Translate and zoom, then permissions, the engine the site opens in, site data and downloads. Drag actions into, along and out of the row on top, or choose them in Edit; each device keeps its own. - On Mac, Site Controls open from the button in the address field. A blocked pop-up, a permission request or Developer Mode waits in its own section with Allow, Deny or Turn Off, instead of replacing the whole panel. - Copy Page Title, Show QR Code and Open Page in Private Window are new commands in the menu bar and the command palette. Show QR Code shows the page's address as a QR code in Site Controls. - Templates start a Space's look, each setting an icon and colors together, and Undo puts back colors a template replaced. New Simple crests, Crest, Moon, Summit, Lens, Spark and Grove, sit beside the Heraldic ones, and new Spaces start in the Crest look. - Give any Space color an exact hex code, or pick it with the system color picker. - After Crest updates, the first window opens the new release's notes on crestbrowser.com in a new tab. - Crest for Mac runs on Intel Macs as well as Apple silicon, as one universal app with its Chromium engine built for both. - Crest for Mac runs on macOS 15 Sequoia and later. On macOS 15, controls that stand on Liquid Glass on macOS 26 stand on Crest's own material instead, and pages translate when you choose Translate rather than automatically.
### Changed
- Crest has a new look: a three-banner mark, warm paper surfaces, Crest blue kept for actions, and Allo, a rounded typeface, for headings, buttons and labels across setup, Settings, the Start Page and Getting Started. The app icon and each alternative icon follow your light, dark, tinted and clear icon style. - The selected tab is a sheet of translucent white, and a selected pin shows its site's color through it. In Settings › Appearance › More Customization you can set how opaque the white is, turn off the pin's tint, or choose Material for the earlier look. - In dark mode, Settings, the space behind pages, Getting Started and the command palette are black and charcoal instead of navy. Setup lies on Crest's navy in light and dark mode. - Panels, prompts, hover previews and notices sit on paper in light mode and on charcoal in dark mode. Crest's own buttons, fields and surfaces replace glass and the system accent color throughout, with one set of shadows and the same hover and press highlights everywhere. - Menus show an icon on every row, and Settings shows solid icons in Crest's colors. - When a page can't read files you chose, or a download starts with the sidebar hidden, Crest says so in the notice at the top of the window instead of an alert or a box in the corner. - A Space's colors are a Background and an Accent, each one color or a gradient of up to three, from a preset or a color wheel with brightness and texture. They replace the Heraldic, Modern and Simple styles. A Space's appearance reads template, then colors, then icon, and choosing a crest, symbol or emoji as the icon keeps the Space's colors. More Customization opens as its own page, with the crest's colors at the top. - Spaces brought in from another browser keep their own icon, set on a round crest in the Space's color. The Space picker shows your Spaces in a well with a lighter mark for Sub-Spaces. - In the command palette, Return searches a phrase or anything else that isn't an address, while one word that starts an open or pinned tab's name or site, or a site you use, goes there. History results show their site's icon with a small clock badge, and the selected row looks like the selected tab, or wears the Space's accent if you turn that on in Appearance. - Animations are quicker throughout, switching Spaces is a little faster, and Peek opens much faster, with Peek animation time in Settings › Links. Cards and controls that appear in place grow from 80% of their size, and every long press takes the same half second. - What's New in Settings › About and on the update card opens the release's notes on crestbrowser.com. - Update notes leave out changes that only reach iPhone and iPad, and link to the release's page. - Download badges show how far your downloads are together, as the Dock does. - Addresses ending in .test count as local everywhere: the developer toolbar turns on for them, and a typed one opens over HTTP first. - Counts such as selected tabs, passwords and downloads in progress follow each language's plural rules.
### Fixed
- Saved, pinned, reopened and imported tabs whose address holds characters such as { or [ return to the exact page they were saved at, instead of a broken search. - An address you type or paste in the command palette opens at the #section you gave it, even on a page you've visited before. - Pages opening in dark mode go straight from the loading screen to the page, without a flash of white in between. - Crest no longer crashes when a page closes while it's loading another site, on Mac in WebKit and on iPhone and iPad. - Scrolling down a sidebar with long open folders no longer jumps back up, and folders inside them no longer shrink to their title and grow again as they scroll into view. - A new window that opens on Getting Started or Settings shows it at once instead of after a blank pause. - Importing another browser's passwords brings those for sites without HTTPS too, and says Crest won't fill them in. - Search provider chips in the command palette show their text in white or black, whichever reads better on the chip's color. - Making a Split View from a single tab asks you to select at least 2 tabs. - When Crest can't save your session, Sync settings says why in plain words instead of an internal code. - A folder or Space without a name is called Untitled Folder or Untitled Space everywhere, including sync. - A page in a language written in another script, such as Traditional Chinese for a reader of Simplified Chinese, is offered translation. - A custom search engine on localhost or a .local name is refused even when it's written with a trailing or full-width dot.
### Security
- Chromium is updated to 158.0.8127.37, with 204 upstream security fixes, six of them critical. Pages in WebKit, and Crest on iPhone and iPad, don't use Chromium.
### Upgrading
- Mac requires macOS 15 Sequoia or later, on Apple silicon or Intel. iPhone and iPad require iOS or iPadOS 26.1 or later.

## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 61 user-facing changes.
### Improved
- Saved passwords and Space choices in Settings show each Space in its own accent colour. - In the command palette, the Pinned & Saved search and the rows for pinned, saved and open tabs wear the same filled symbols as their sections in the sidebar. - Translation, the emoji picker, the viewport preview and the sidebar width preview use Crest blue instead of the Mac's system accent colour. - The downloads badge, and on iPhone and iPad the private browsing button, take the Space's accent colour, so they stand out from the sidebar behind them. - The sample page in the zoom and appearance settings is ink on Crest's warm paper, and the globe engine mark on tabs and in the site engine menu is Crest blue. - Extension badges are Crest's red with slightly larger text, and pinned extension buttons use the same hover highlight as Crest's other toolbar buttons. - Search fields in Settings, the sidebar's lists, folder previews and the icon and symbol pickers share one look, show a focus ring while you type, and have a clear button that highlights under the pointer. - The developer toolbar's buttons, the extension side panel's close button and the engine choices in Settings highlight under the pointer like Crest's other controls, and disclosure arrows in site settings and Privacy point the right way in right-to-left languages. - The sidebar's update and Now Playing cards, the translation bar and the symbol and emoji pickers use Crest's standard buttons, with the same hover and press highlights as the rest of Crest. - Reviewing a password import shows the Space's crest and lays the totals, accounts, warnings and rejected rows out in Settings-style groups, with each row number tagged in its warning or error colour. - Renaming a Space in place shows Crest's field with a focus ring, and its pencil highlights under the pointer. - Link routes in Settings sit directly in their group instead of a box inside it, the URL pattern uses Crest's field with a focus ring, and the route actions button highlights under the pointer.

## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 14 user-facing changes.
### New
- Collapse All Folders closes every open folder in a Space at once, nested folders included, without closing any tabs. Find it in the Space's menu, in the sidebar's menu and the View menu on Mac, and in the command palette.
### Improved
- Clear now keeps the tab you're on and archives your other open tabs. On Mac, hold Option to turn it into Clear All. Clear All Tabs, Option-Shift-Command-K, is also in the Tabs menu, the command palette and the Space's ••• menu, which is where iPhone and iPad find it. - Large folders open about twice as fast, with the folders inside them filling in just after, and a folder's preview on Mac appears without a pause even when it holds hundreds of tabs. - Folders brought in from another browser now arrive closed, nested ones included, so a large import opens to a tidy sidebar. Folders from a Crest backup keep how you left them. - On Mac, with the address bar in the sidebar, pages in Split View no longer each carry their own bar along the top: the sidebar's serves the page you're on, as it does for a single page. With the address bar on top, each page keeps its own. - Settings › Tabs now lets you choose separately what pinned tabs and saved tabs do after you close them, so saved tabs can go back to their saved URL while pinned tabs resume where you left off. Your current choice carries over to both.
### Fixed
- On iPhone and iPad, tapping a folder in the sidebar opens or closes it again instead of bringing up its preview. Holding a folder still shows the preview. - Folder icons wider than a folder, such as a computer or a group of people, now show whole in the sidebar instead of cut off at their edge. - Chromium Spaces can open devices on your local network, such as routers, NAS drives and home servers, once you turn on Crest Helper under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network, now Crest's own setting rather than one shared with other apps. A page that can't reach a local address says how to allow it instead of reporting a refused connection. - In Chromium Spaces, an http:// address you type or open now stays on HTTP, including when you reload it, instead of being switched to HTTPS. Links on pages still try HTTPS first and fall back to HTTP when a site doesn't offer it. - Files downloaded over plain HTTP in Chromium Spaces are no longer blocked outright: Crest asks whether to keep them, as it does for other risky downloads. - When you type a site without http:// or https://, Crest tries HTTPS first and opens it over HTTP if HTTPS can't reach it. Local addresses, such as nas.lan:5000 or a device name with a port, open over HTTP right away, and an address you type with https:// never falls back.

## Highlights
### New
- A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.
### Improved
- Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.
### Fixed
- Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit. - A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs. - A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open. - Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share. - Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder. - Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.
